source.title: Leveraging Random Label Memorization for Unsupervised Pre-Training
source.authors: Vinaychandran Pondenkandath; Michele Alberti; Sammer Puran; R. Ingold; M. Liwicki

page_placements.theme: Prior training changes subsequent memorization and transfer

record.tranche_reason: The study trains C3D networks on randomly labeled video datasets and reports a training-accuracy result, using a different setting from the original sources.
record.gate_note: Figure 1 reports training accuracy during sequential label reshuffling. Downstream validation accuracies after random-label pre-training are also reported, but they do not measure the claim versions directly. The cited findings from Zhang et al. and Li et al. are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: Figure 1 reports the study's own random-label training accuracy in a video-network setting, bearing on V1. The supplied text does not establish zero or near-zero training error. Downstream transfer accuracy and faster repeated memorization do not test the other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the conclusion: the authors interpret their preliminary transfer gains as evidence that random-label pre-training can learn useful representations and recommend further research. Their conclusion describes gains of 1–5% accuracy; the tables specifically show 0.8, 1.7, and 5.2 percentage points.
record.recipe_differences: Uses 3D C3D video models, random-label pre-training, then fine-tuning on a separate correctly labeled dataset; reports downstream classification accuracy rather than direct fit and test error on random labels.
record.method_sensitivity: Pre-training dataset and evaluation dataset vary; the paper reports different downstream accuracies across these settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Random-label pre-training improves downstream validation accuracy by 0.8, 1.7, and 5.2 percentage points in the reported settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random-label pre-training can improve subsequent supervised video classification.

fits_no_version.finding: After labels are reshuffled, subsequent memorization proceeds faster than the initial round from random weights.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prior random-label training accelerates subsequent random-label memorization in the same network.

record.peer_reviewed: Workshop of Integration of Deep Learning Theories at Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NIPS) 2018
record.problems: The paper provides no numeric training accuracy or training error for the random-label fitting result; Figure 1 is the only result for repeated memorization and is presented as a plot. No uncertainty estimates are stated.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training error cannot be established from the supplied figure text; chance-level test performance and unchanged hyperparameters relative to true-label training are not reported.
Random-label versus true-label fitting time and convergence as corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training fit and test-error trajectories across fractions of label corruption.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization. The future-work speculation supplies no test.
Learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noise, and comparative real-label versus random-label learning dynamics.

record.verdict_notes: No V1 verdict is justified without a readable fitting endpoint. Missing figure values are an evidence-access limitation for R1, not evidence that fitting fails. The study is not an original source for these versions.

versions.untested_parts: The text does not state whether training error reaches zero or near zero, the resulting test error, or whether the same architecture and training hyperparameters are retained relative to a true-label training baseline.

rows.subject: C3D
rows.operation_detail: Training on randomly labeled data, then reshuffling labels after a fixed amount of epochs and restarting memorization.

conditions.value: sequentially re-shuffling the set of labels

rows.measure: Training accuracy during successive memorization processes
rows.note: The text says subsequent memorization processes are much faster than the initial one, but does not state training accuracy values or explicitly say it reaches zero.
rows.check: The supplied text contains the figure caption but no readable accuracy values or explicit near-perfect fitting result. Section 3.3 does not identify the experiment's dataset or explicitly identify its network as C3D. Faster subsequent memorization compares random-label training rounds, not random versus true labels.

rows.subject: C3D
rows.operation_detail: Pre-trained on randomly labeled UCF-101, then fine-tuned with correct labels on HMDB51.
rows.note: Downstream transfer result; it does not measure a claim version's named outcome.
rows.check: The reported 17.4% to 18.2% downstream validation gain is correct, but cannot establish any claim version's effect. Retain only as an auxiliary transfer result.

rows.subject: C3D
rows.operation_detail: Pre-trained on randomly labeled HMDB51, then fine-tuned with correct labels on UCF-101.
rows.note: Downstream transfer result; it does not measure a claim version's named outcome.
rows.check: The reported 32.9% to 34.6% downstream validation gain is correct, but cannot establish any claim version's effect. Retain only as an auxiliary transfer result.

rows.subject: C3D
rows.operation_detail: Pre-trained on a randomly labeled subset of Sports-1M, then evaluated on Kinetics.
rows.note: Downstream transfer result; it does not measure a claim version's named outcome.
rows.check: The reported 35.0% to 40.2% downstream validation gain is correct, but cannot establish any claim version's effect. The operation should explicitly include fine-tuning on correctly labeled Kinetics.

rows.subject: C3D
rows.operation_detail: Pre-trained on correctly labeled Sports-1M, then evaluated on Kinetics.
rows.check: The 69.8% value is a correctly labeled pre-training comparator for the study's transfer method, not a random-label fitting result. It uses the complete Sports-1M dataset, whereas R4 uses roughly 40%, and includes subsequent Kinetics training.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The study reports its own sequential random-label memorization experiment, beyond using memorization for pre-training.

tranche.reason: Figure 1 and Section 3.3 report random-label training behavior in a video-network setting, bearing on V1; downstream transfer results alone do not test the versions.

source_check.notes: Figure 1 provides no textual numeric training accuracies establishing zero or near-zero training error. R2 and R3 are auxiliary downstream transfer results and correctly have no version links.
